spiderweb_pins.note: Local compilation package; the source records no upstream agency, URL or date, so the pins are a name and an approximate location only. The origin labels them T2; the recorded provenance supports T4. Coordinates are stated at 2-3 decimals in that source (roughly 100 m to 1 km).

source_service_notes.note: echo_rest_services.get_facilities silently ignores the p_naics filter: p_naics=562212 and p_naics=999999 both returned all 15256 Puerto Rico rows with Message=Success. p_sic filters correctly. Every ECHO query therefore carries a filtered-versus-unfiltered control.

case_rest_services.get_cases honours p_state, p_region and p_case_number and silently drops every other parameter tried (p_case_name, p_fed_state, p_st, p_epa_region, p_fac_state, p_case_state, p_cs_state, p_zip): combined with p_state the result is unchanged, alone it is refused. With no honoured filter the service refuses the query and reports the unfiltered total in its error message. get_case_info ignores p_id and p_activity_id and returns the whole-service summary. All name and NAICS filtering is therefore done locally on the complete p_state pull, and the state filter carries a control (a nonsense state returns 0 rows; the filtered count is below the unfiltered total).

Most case rows have no NAICS code (3108 of 3788 in the Puerto Rico pull), so a NAICS filter alone would silently miss most landfill cases. Case rows carry no facility id or coordinates, so a case can be linked to a site by name only, except where an ECHO facility report lists the case number as one of its own source ids.
